newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Talks on Colombian port strike end in deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Talks on Colombian port strike end in deadlock.

text.p: Talks aimed at ending a week-old dockworkers' strike in Colombia's Pacific port of Buenaventura ended in a deadlock early Wednesday, negotiators said.

Nelson Amaya, regional head of Unitary Workers' Confederation, said the talks in the southwest city of Cali broke down after an 11-hour bargaining session in which operators and port officials had tentatively agreed on a doubling of cargo handling rates.
The talks were set to resume at about 1100 local/1600 GMT, Amaya said.

The port of Buenaventura, shipping point for about 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports and all of its sugar exports, is estimated to be losing $500,000 for every day it is shut down by the job action.
More than 300,000 60-kg bags of coffee earmarked for export, and at least 27,000 tonnes of sugar, have been held up by the strike, according to port authorities and exporters.
In addition to wage hikes, the 3,000 port workers in Buenaventura are demanding additional payments for social security along with sickness and injury benefits.
